AMZN · SEC CIK 0001018724 Amazon.com, Inc. is a retail business that runs on our stores to enable hundreds of millions of unique products to be sold by us and by third parties across dozens of product categories. Its position is contested less by a named firm than by the alternatives its customers already have: customers can substitute publishers, distributors and the shopper buying the same basket somewhere cheaper, and the economics that decide the contest are moderate operating leverage — a largely fixed store and distribution base against thin unit margin, so small comparable-sales moves swing profit. Public intelligence — what it could establish Amazon.com, Inc. is a retail business that runs on our stores to enable hundreds of millions of unique products to be sold by us and by third parties across dozens of product categories. The reading follows from how this kind of business works; 1 source(s) outside the company's control were read, which is not enough to size the effect, so it is held in direction only. 1 of the passages read came from a source the company does not control. Internal intelligence — what is still bounded These are the measures a business of this kind is judged on that the public record did not supply. Each one is a magnitude the analysis above had to leave in direction only. comparable sales, split into traffic and basket — thin margin means small comparable moves swing profit. gross margin and markdown rate — buying scale and inventory discipline show up here first. inventory turns — the return in this model comes from turns, not from price premium. cost of goods and sourcing terms — the buying side is where a discounter's advantage is made. membership, advertising and other high-margin income — the part of profit that does not come from selling goods. What can be connected Connected now Public filings and disclosures Regulatory filings, the company's own pages, and independent sources — everything the analysis you just read was built from. Available next Your documents Board packs, strategy decks and plans. The system reads what management actually decided rather than inferring it from the outside. Available next Financial plan and internal metrics The numbers the public record does not contain — the ones that turn every bounded magnitude above into a measured one. What impossible hypothesis should we tes.text: Home · Your analyses · Guest demo session Leave demo Amazon.com, Inc. What impossible hypothesis should we test? The workflow that Amazon.com, Inc.'s product sits inside may stop existing rather than be improved.: It sells its stores to enable hundreds of millions of unique products to be sold by us and by third parties across dozens of product categories. A product priced against a human process captures a share of that process's cost; when the process is performed by a machine end to end, the customer is no longer buying a better way to do it, and there is nothing left for the price to be a share of.; Amazon.com, Inc.'s most important competitor may be its own customers deciding to do this themselves.: It charges on interchange and other fees, which may increase over time and raise its operating costs and lower profitability. A charge that scales with the customer's own volume grows into a line item large enough to justify a build, and the largest customers reach that threshold first — which are the same accounts the revenue depends on most.; publishers may be structurally unable to answer a move here, which would make the contested position far cheaper to take than a symmetric reading implies.: publishers was established as a competitor from disclosure rather than assumed.
